{{short description|French mathematician}}
[[File:Henrion - Usage du compas de proportion, 1637 - BEIC 218820 F.jpg|thumb|''Usage du compas de proportion'', 1637 ]]
'''Denis''' (sometimes Didier) '''Henrion''', was a French [[mathematician]] born at the end of the 16th century in France.<ref>{{cite book|last=Mottelay|first=Paul Fleury |title=Bibliographical History of Electricity and Magnetism|year=2008|publisher=Read Books|isbn=978-1-4437-2844-7|page=109}}</ref> He co-edited the works of [[Viète]]. He died around 1632 in Paris.

== Contributions ==

Henrion wrote a tract concerning [[logarithm]]s.<ref>{{citation|journal=The London, Edinburgh, and Dublin Philosophical Magazine and Journal of Science|volume=44|year=1872|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=O55YAAAAcAAJ&pg=PA500|authorlink=James Whitbread Lee Glaisher|first=J. W. L.|last=Glaisher|title=Supplementary remarks on some early logarithmic tables}}. Glaisher writes that Henrion, [[Adriaan Vlacq]], and [[Ezechiel de Decker]] were rivals for being "the first foreigner who published Briggian logarithms"; he notes Henrion's ''Traicté des Logarithmes'' (Paris, 1926).</ref> 

He translated [[Euclid's Elements]] from Latin into French.

He published ''Problemata nobilissima duo'' (Paris, 1616), a book against [[Marin Ghetaldi]] and attacking [[François Viète|Viète]] and [[Regiomontanus]]. Later reorganized, the book was republished by its author.

== Works (selection) ==
=== Original works ===
* [https://books.google.com/books?id=1qBEAAAAcAAJ ''Mémoires mathématiques recueillis et dressés en faveur de la noblesse française'']. Paris, 1613, 4°. Published again in Paris by Fleury Bourriquant, 1623, 8°
* ''Problemata duo nobilissima, quorum nec analysin geometricam, videntur tenuisse [[Regiomontanus|Ioannes Regiomontanus]] & [[Petrus Nonius]]; nec demonstrationem satis accuratam repraesentasse, [[François Viète|Franciscus Vieta]] et [[Marin Ghetaldi|Marinus Ghetaldus]] nunc demum a Clemente Cyriaco diligentius elaborata et novis analyseon formis exculta. Inscriptiones praeterea figurarum non injucundœ''. Paris: David Leclerc, 1616, 4°. ([https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_TWZp7hVzexIC Internet Archive link])
* ''Problematum opus amplissimum et schediasmata poetica et critica'' (manuscript)
* [http://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k62780715 ''Deux cens questions ingénieuses et récréatives extraictes et tirées des œuvres mathématiques de Valentin Menher avec quelques annotations de Michel Coignet, le tout corrigé, recueilli et mis en cet ordre, par D.H.P.E.M.'']<ref>"D.H.P.E.M" stands for "Denis Henrion, professeur ès mathématiques"</ref> Paris, 1620
* [https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_FgMOAAAAQAAJ ''L'usage du mécomètre, qui est un instrument géométrique avec lequel on peut très facilement mesurer toutes sortes de longueurs et distances visibles'']. Paris, 1630, 8°

=== Translations ===
* ''Les Quinze livres des Éléments d'Euclide, traduits du latin en français''. Online: [https://books.google.com/books?id=skt1Zd_SFUgC&pg=PR1 ''Tables des directions et projections de Jean de Mont-Royal'']<ref>"Jean de Mont-Royal" is Regiomontanus.</ref>
